source.title: A note-question on partitions of semigroups

accepted.question_text: Let G be a group, and let P be a partition of G into n cells. For a subset A of G, write AA^{-1} = {ab^{-1} : a,b ∈ A}. Must there exist a cell A ∈ P and a subset F ⊆ G with |F| ≤ n such that every element of G lies in FAA^{-1}, that is, G = FAA^{-1}?

evidence.quote: In 1995, the first author asked the following question [3, Problem 13.44]. Given a group G and an n-partition P, n ∈ N of G, do there exist A ∈ P and a subset F of G such that G = F AA−1 and |F| ≤ n?

For the current state of this open problem see the survey [1]. We mention only that an answer is positive if either G is amenable (in particular, finite), or n ≤ 3, or x−1Ax = A for any A ∈ P and x ∈ G.

accepted.question_text: Let S be a semigroup, and let P be a partition of S into n cells. For a subset A ⊆ S, define Δ(A) = {x ∈ S : xA ∩ A ≠ ∅}. For subsets X,B ⊆ S, write X^{-1}B = ⋃_{x∈X} {y ∈ S : xy ∈ B}. When S^{-1}Δ(A) = S, define the covering number of Δ(A) by covΔ(A) = min{|X| : X ⊆ S and S = X^{-1}Δ(A)}. Must there exist a cell A ∈ P such that covΔ(A) ≤ n?

evidence.quote: We set ∆(A) = {x ∈ S : xA ∩ A 6= ∅} and observe that ∆(A) = {x ∈ S : x−1A ∩ A 6= ∅} and if S is a group then ∆(A) = AA−1.
We suppose that S−1A = S and define a covering number covA = min{|X| : X ⊆ S, S = X−1A}.
Now we are ready for promised question. Given a semigroup S and an n-partition P of S, does there exist A ∈ P such that cov∆(A) ≤ n?
We give an affirmative answer provided that either S is finite or n = 2.
